_comment: Separation-of-duties policy for scripts/toxic_combinations.py and .ps1. Each rule lists two or more sides; a user who satisfies EVERY side is a finding. A side is any_of (one match is enough) or all_of (needs every entry). Entry types: app (label, name or id), app_group (an app only when it comes through a specific group), group (name or id), admin_role (role type such as SUPER_ADMIN, a role label, or a custom role id), no_phishing_resistant_factor. List the access you would rather KEEP first: when two fixes cost the same, the tool suggests changing the side listed last. exceptions = logins or user ids that are approved to hold the combination (documented break-glass accounts etc.).

rules.name: Okta super admin without phishing-resistant MFA
rules.why: A phished password plus a pushed or typed code is enough to take over the whole Okta tenant.

rules.name: AWS production admin who is also a finance approver
rules.why: One person could both run up cloud spend and approve the invoices for it.

rules.name: Creates vendors and approves payments
rules.why: Classic payment fraud: set up a fake vendor, then approve its invoices.

rules.name: Grants admin rights and reviews them
rules.why: Someone who can hand out admin roles should not also certify who has them.
